#301
The heat map is a consequence comparison, not a probability map. Its central result is that the compound shock can defeat all modules simultaneously, while otherwise distinct scenarios repeatedly stress coordination and remedy. The common corrective priority is therefore a tested decision chain, not another general statement that cyber risk is important.
#302
Early indicators. Signals include privileged-access anomalies; key-policy exceptions; unresolved reconciliation breaks; vendor or cloud concentration; repeated high-severity vulnerabilities; fraudulent domain and social-media impersonation; abrupt withdrawal or complaint spikes; delayed incident classification; inconsistent public statements; unavailable decision-makers; evidence-transfer failures; and orders that cannot be implemented by custodians or foreign platforms.
#303
Residual risk and implication. No architecture prevents every theft, outage or fraud. Foreign recovery may fail, technical intervention may be unavailable, and compensation may not cover loss. The design implication is to minimise irreversible exposure, preserve lawful options and practise failure. Uncertainty: the initiating event, target, duration, asset-recovery rate and contagion path cannot be predicted and are not assigned probabilities.

26.17.10 Cross-border fragmentation or harmonisation

#304
Assumption. Foreign jurisdictions continue to implement crypto-asset, stablecoin, tax, payment, sanctions, data and AI rules at different speeds. Some requirements converge through international standards while market-access, custody, issuer, privacy and enforcement rules remain incompatible. Pakistan may face both demands for recognition and restrictions by foreign providers.
#305
The scenario stresses section 4 extraterritorial reach and sections 9 and 17 cooperation and recognition powers. An offshore platform may target Pakistan without a conventional establishment; a foreign issuer may serve local wallets but deny local jurisdiction; or a Pakistan licensee may depend on a custodian whose home regulator restricts service. Two authorities may demand inconsistent retention, disclosure, freezing or customer treatment. A memorandum can facilitate exchange but cannot create coercive power or extinguish a Pakistani remedy.
#306
The FSB’s 2025 review identifies gaps and inconsistencies in implementation and the resulting opportunity for regulatory arbitrage.75 FATF’s revised Recommendation 16 increases convergence around payment-message information, but international convergence does not itself decide Pakistan’s domestic authority, privacy safeguards or technical interface.76 Tax reporting adds another lane: CARF-style exchange requires domestic fiscal authority, due diligence, secure systems and an international legal basis, not a PVARA licence alone.
#307
the corrective programme’s issue-specific recognition model is robust if every reliance decision identifies the activity, comparable outcome, home supervisor, data and record access, customer-asset location, local service and complaint route, enforcement cooperation, transition and withdrawal. Recognition should reduce duplicate evidence only where cooperation works. Material retail, custody, payment or stablecoin exposure may require local conditions even when a foreign licence is respected for a limited function.
#308
The contrary path—fragmentation—requires an exit playbook. PVARA should be able to identify affected customers, assets, dependencies and contractual rights; require notice and transfer; preserve records; coordinate with SBP, FMU, tax and enforcement bodies; and state what Pakistan can and cannot compel. An untested promise of international cooperation is not a safeguard.
#309
Early indicators. The dashboard should track foreign legal changes affecting Pakistan access; rejected supervisory requests; delayed or incomplete Travel Rule messages; foreign licence restrictions; concentration in jurisdictions without effective cooperation; conflicts over data, sanctions or freezes; sudden terms-of-service changes; blocked redemptions or withdrawals; and growing targeted solicitation by unregistered offshore providers.
#310
Residual risk and implication. Pakistan cannot harmonise foreign law unilaterally and should not trade away constitutional, monetary, tax or customer-protection requirements for nominal access. The design implication is selective interoperability with an executable withdrawal route. Uncertainty: foreign reforms, equivalence decisions, geopolitical conditions and provider cooperation are external variables; neither harmonisation nor fragmentation is presumed dominant.

26.17.11 Mining, energy and environmental pathway

#311
The detailed legal treatment of mining, electricity connection, tariff, curtailment, metering, grid effects, environmental cost and public-resource allocation belongs with the technical and fiscal analysis in Chapter 4 § 4.7 and Chapter 13. For anticipatory purposes, Chapter 26 retains the governing test: no claim of surplus power or public benefit should be accepted without temporal grid evidence, lawful allocation of public resources, fiscal transparency, environmental measurement, reversible permission and a reasoned decision by the competent authorities. The scenario programme should monitor load concentration, curtailment stress, subsidy exposure, emissions, water use, local distribution and the opportunity cost of alternative public uses.

26.17.12 Rights and distribution under the scenarios

#312
None of the scenarios is distributionally neutral. The same control can protect one interest and burden another. Enhanced traceability may reduce fraud but expose financial associations; a rapid freeze may preserve assets but restrict innocent property; high capital requirements may protect customers but concentrate the market; local-presence rules may improve remedy but exclude a useful foreign service; and mining revenue may benefit one region while electricity or environmental cost falls elsewhere.
#313
The constitutional frame remains legality, fair treatment, privacy and dignity, economic freedom subject to law, property, equality, information, federal distribution of authority and effective judicial review. These rights do not decide every policy outcome, but they require lawful source, rational classification, proportionality where rights are restricted, reasons and remedy.78

#314
The rights test must occur at design and incident stages. A lawful data field can become disproportionate when retained indefinitely or shared for a new purpose. An emergency restriction can become unlawful when urgency ends. An algorithmic risk score can support triage but should not become an undisclosed reason for licence refusal, account closure or enforcement. Human review must have authority and enough information to change the result.
#315
Distribution should also be measured by who can exit. A sophisticated institution may diversify custodians, verify reserves and litigate abroad; a retail user may rely on a phone interface and regulatory badge. the corrective programme’s portability, reasons and remedy controls therefore protect capability, not merely formal equality. The National Digital Masterplan framework can coordinate inclusion and infrastructure, but it cannot authorise sector regulation or override rights.79
#316
Cross-scenario implication. The dashboard should disaggregate complaints, losses, freezes, service interruptions, licensing outcomes and remediation where lawful and statistically responsible. It should test whether burdens cluster by customer type, region, gender, disability, business size or access channel without turning protected data into a new risk. Uncertainty: distributional effects depend on actual use and institutional behaviour; no inclusion or employment benefit is presumed.

26.17.13 Decision triggers and early indicators

#317
Anticipatory intelligence becomes useful only when an indicator is connected to a lawful decision. A dashboard that reports rising stablecoin use but does not identify who can act, under what provision, with what evidence and remedy is market commentary, not governance. The the corrective programme implementation register should therefore add a scenario field to each corrective item: which future condition it protects against, what signal activates review and what response is available before primary law changes.
#318
For this dashboard, three operational levels are proposed. Watch means an indicator changed and its lead must verify source and context. Escalate means an adopted threshold or qualitative condition has been met and responsible institutions must assess exposure and options. Act means the legal condition for a defined intervention has been proved. A trigger never invents power. Where authority is absent, the response is amendment, court process, referral to the competent institution or limitation of a voluntary programme.

#319
The threshold for an indicator should be adopted by the institution with legal and technical competence. Some can be numerical—capital, reconciliation tolerance or outage impact—once evidence exists. Others are necessarily qualitative: loss of a lawful decision-maker, inability to identify the holder’s claim, or conflict between two binding commands. The dashboard should show source, data quality, version and the reason an alert was opened or closed.

26.17.14 No-regret moves

#320
Eight measures improve resilience across every scenario without presuming which one occurs:
maintain a public, versioned register of legal instruments, permissions, decisions and institutional authority;
make the PVARA–SBP–SECP–FMU perimeter and incident routes operational through test cases;
require reconstructable customer assets, liabilities, keys and dependencies, with an exercised return plan;
establish interoperable AML/Travel Rule and sanctions processes with privacy, correction and protected access;
authenticate the Tribunal, investigation and urgent-review routes before coercive crisis action;
record concentration in providers, banks, custodians, cloud, analytics, bridges, oracles and AI models;
run compound exercises that include legal, customer, communication, evidence and cross-border failure; and
publish outcome evidence and residual risk so that scale, restriction or legislative correction is reasoned.
#321
These moves implement rather than enlarge the corrective programme. Their legal basis must still be identified item by item.80 They should be reviewed quarterly at programme level, immediately after a material event and independently after the first full operational cycle. The review should preserve false alarms and rejected evidence; otherwise the State cannot learn whether its indicators are useful.

26.18 Public Outcomes, Evidence and Accountability

26.18.1 Access, integrity, stability, innovation and rights

#322
Success is not the number of licences or transaction volume. Relevant outcomes include safe access, market integrity, customer-asset recovery, payment resilience, lawful innovation, tax compliance, financial inclusion and protected rights. Trade-offs should be reported rather than hidden in a composite score.

26.18.2 Metrics, independent review and legal learning

#323
PVARA should publish time-to-decision, refusal and appeal outcomes, complaints, asset shortfalls, incidents, enforcement disposition and market concentration with necessary confidentiality. Independent review should test both legality and effect. Lessons should lead to reasons, consultation and instrument change—not silent modification of forms or software.

26.18.3 Digital Nation finance-sector implementation plan and constitutional tests

#324
The responsible federal Division should prepare a digital-assets sectoral implementation plan for Commission approval and Masterplan alignment. The plan should identify statutory outcomes, reform modules, owners, dependencies, resources, procurement, common infrastructure, indicators, risks, public reporting and review. PVARA, SBP, SECP, FMU, FBR, Law Division, relevant investigation bodies, provinces and the PDA should contribute within their mandates.
#325
Each proposed national initiative should pass the twelve constitutional planning tests developed in Chapter 6: source of authority; lawful institution; federal–provincial competence; rights; public finance; procurement; data; cyber; regulatory perimeter; remedies; evidence; and revision. A label such as “national wallet”, “tokenised government asset”, “strategic reserve” or “mining hub” supplies none of those answers.

26.18.4 Separating regulatory foundations from market initiatives

#326
The plan should contain two portfolios. The regulatory-foundation portfolio covers the amendment Bill, Rules, final Regulations, appointments, Tribunal, registers, interfaces, standards, capacity and tests. The market and public-use portfolio covers sandbox projects, tokenisation, payments, mining, investment promotion or public-sector uses. No initiative in the second portfolio should pass its scale gate until the applicable first-portfolio dependencies are complete.
#327
For public-sector tokenisation or wallet use, the sponsoring institution must identify the legal asset, public-money flow, custodian, procurement, accounting, audit, cybersecurity, data, customer or citizen remedy, failure allocation and exit. A pilot should cap exposure and preserve an off-chain authoritative record where law requires. The State should not use a sandbox to avoid fiscal, procurement or constitutional control.

26.18.5 Aligning indicators with public outcomes

#328
National reporting should distinguish inputs, outputs, operational outcomes and public outcomes. Staff hired and regulations issued are inputs and outputs. Accurate status, secure customer assets, reduced unresolved complaints, effective detection, predictable decisions, service recovery and lawful tax reporting are operational outcomes. Financial inclusion, investment quality, innovation, lower cross-border friction and reduced illicit finance are public outcomes that require evidence and counterfactual care.
#329
The plan should publish baselines, definitions, source systems, frequency, owner and limitations. Commercial market estimates and chain-analytics outputs should be labelled as estimates. Regulatory data should not be repurposed for publicity without legal basis and quality review. The Commission’s monitoring record should disclose delayed dependencies and corrective decisions rather than convert every indicator into a success narrative.
#330
At the evidence cut-off, official federal reporting described National Digital Masterplan consultations and implementation-roadmap work as ongoing. That supports active alignment work, not an inference that a final Commission-approved sector plan already exists.58 the corrective programme therefore recommends the legal home and approval route; it does not invent approval.

26.18.6 Controlled reconciliation of 27 audit items, 24 issues and 25 gaps

#331
The register reconciles, without conflating, the 27-item audit, 24 workbook issues and 25 missing-instrument gaps. These are research controls, not law. Chapters 5–17 refine their findings; the permitted dispositions are amend, regulate, coordinate, study, monitor and accept.59

Closure requires the stated proof.
#333
Some residual risks may be accepted, monitored or studied where law is valid, safeguards operate and reasons are recorded. Unresolved authority, customer ownership, coercive process, tax, institutional validity and remedy remain legality gates. Scale should follow operating evidence, not innovation vocabulary.

26.19 The Final Proposition

26.19.1 A digital-asset order worthy of code, law and capital

#334
Code can represent transactions and assist compliance; law allocates authority, rights and remedies; capital supplies productive risk-bearing. A credible order holds all three together. It allows innovation only through valid institutions and protects citizens without treating technological novelty as suspicion or immunity.

26.19.2 Authority remains human, public and legally accountable

#335
The final safeguard is institutional responsibility. Legislatures enact; authorised regulators decide; courts adjudicate; firms remain accountable for their systems; citizens receive reasons and remedies. No dashboard, model, outsourced service or protocol should displace that chain. Pakistan's future order should become more intelligible through technology and remain governed by law.

26.19.3 Bottom line and eight governing design principles

#336
Pakistan does not need another declaration that digital assets matter. It needs a controlled conversion of enacted law into an operable legal order. The Virtual Assets Act 2026 (VAA) has already supplied a federal regulator, a functional service perimeter, licensing and issuer modules, customer-asset duties, preventive and supervisory powers, offences, an appellate design and delegated-law powers. The preceding chapters nevertheless show that enactment and operability are not the same thing. A statute can be in force while the entry route is transitional, the final rulebook remains incomplete, a cross-regulator boundary is unresolved, an institution has not been authenticated, or a remedy cannot yet be exercised predictably.30
#337
The corrective package therefore begins from law already enacted. It does not treat the field as a clean slate, reproduce the Act in subordinate legislation or replace specialised regulators with a digital-asset super-regulator. It also does not ask regulated businesses to cure defects that belong to the State. A VASP can file a complete application, segregate customer assets and implement controls. It cannot appoint the Authority’s Board, establish a Tribunal, correct a statutory cross-reference, create a tax charge, allocate federal and provincial competence, or convert draft regulations into law. Those tasks must remain with the institutions legally empowered to perform them.
#338
Eight principles govern the programme.
Legality before scale. No market-expansion target, public-wallet programme, mining allocation or tokenisation initiative should outrun the legal authority, customer protection, fiscal control and review mechanism applicable to it.
Instrument discipline. Parliament should decide essential policy, jurisdiction, coercive power, liability, tax and remedy. Federal Rules and PVARA Regulations should operationalise authority already conferred. Standards may specify testable technical requirements. Guidance may explain but must not create a disguised offence, licence condition or tax burden.
Function before label. The perimeter should turn on the legal and economic function actually performed, including control of assets, order execution, settlement, issuance, payment, investment intermediation and governance—not on names such as “utility token”, “protocol”, “DAO” or “decentralised”.
One decision, visible contributors. Where several regulators participate, one lawful decision-owner must be identifiable. Consultation does not transfer statutory power, and board membership does not merge mandates.
Transition without legal fiction. Continuity should protect customers and enable orderly applications. It should not imply that an NOC is a full licence, that a pending application is approved, or that a saved instrument is automatically valid for every Act-era purpose.
Proof, not promulgation alone. A Gazette notification is necessary where law requires it; it is not evidence that the regulated interface works. Completion requires authenticated instruments, named owners, working forms and data channels, trained decision-makers, tested remedies and published performance evidence.
Proportionality with a hard protective floor. Requirements may vary with activity, scale and risk, but segregation, governance, fitness, financial crime controls, truthful disclosure, operational resilience, reasons and access to review are not optional.
Revision by evidence. The regime should record incidents, supervisory findings, complaints, appeal outcomes, market concentration and implementation failures, and use them to revise subordinate instruments without concealing the version history.
#339
This hierarchy is also a sequencing rule. An administrative form cannot cure missing statutory authority. A memorandum cannot decide a legal perimeter entrusted to Parliament or another regulator. A technical standard cannot impose a penalty not authorised by the Act. Conversely, Parliament need not hard-code every cryptographic control or data field. The reform succeeds when each question is placed at the lowest level that can lawfully and durably answer it, while every higher-order safeguard remains intact.31

Chapter 26 Conclusion and Standalone Contribution

#340
Pakistan's 2026 Act and notified Regulations are a genuine legal foundation, but the public task is unfinished. Construction now means making transition precise, completing primary law, issuing final permissions, protecting customer assets, resolving institutional interfaces and testing outcomes. The sequence is legality, capability, operation, review and measured scale. It neither promises an already functioning regime nor understates the authority that valid instruments presently carry.

Chapter 26 Selected Authorities and Independent-Use Note

#341
This chapter may be read independently as an implementation and institutional-design paper. Its propositions distinguish current law from recommended construction. Before publication, the appeal-routing sentence in § 26.13.2 should receive final source clearance against the official consolidated Constitution then in force; that verification does not alter the chapter's core proposition that statutory review must conform to the Constitution.

Chapter 26 — Building Pakistan’s Digital-Asset Order

Chapter Summary

Pakistan's Virtual Assets Act 2026 and notified PVARA Regulations establish the current legal baseline, but legislation and notification do not by themselves produce an operational market order. This chapter specifies the remaining construction: an authenticated public legal record, lawful transition for incumbents and holders, primary-law completion, activity licensing, monetary and securities interfaces, property and insolvency rules, financial integrity, fiscal treatment, data and cyber controls, institutional responsibility, constitutional review, machine-readable regulation and phased evaluation. It rejects implied amnesty and fictional institutional capacity. The result is a legally sequenced programme in which authority, data, resources, accountability and evidence move together.

Chapter 26 Conclusion

Chapter 26 Authorities and Footnotes

> Proposition. Pakistan has enacted a statutory and regulatory foundation, not a fully operational digital-asset order. Completion requires valid instruments, public transition rules, capable institutions, protected customer assets, coherent monetary and market interfaces, due process and measurable implementation. Technology may represent and test rules; public authority must remain human, lawful and contestable.

Keywords: Pakistan; PVARA; transition; licensing; customer assets; institutional design; implementation; machine-readable regulation.

Research question: What legal and institutional steps are required to convert Pakistan's enacted baseline into a lawful, operational and accountable digital-asset order?

Principal contribution: A construction sequence that distinguishes legal validity, operational capability and evaluated public outcomes, with express treatment of current holders, incumbent providers and review.

Jurisdiction and legal cut-off: Pakistan, stated to 22 August 2026. The Virtual Assets Act 2026 and notified PVARA Virtual Asset Services Regulations 2026 and Activity-Specific Regulations 2026 are treated as the current baseline. Earlier consultation drafts are legislative history only.

26.1 Construction, Not Assumed Reform

26.1.1 Why Pakistan is completing an incomplete order rather than repairing a mature one

The Virtual Assets Act 2026 created the Pakistan Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, defined regulated functions and conferred rulemaking, licensing, supervisory and enforcement powers.ch26-26-1 The notified Regulations add an operative licensing and conduct baseline.ch26-26-2 Yet Pakistan did not inherit a mature, fully licensed market with settled custody, tax, insolvency and inter-regulator practice. The proper verb is construction: bringing law, institutions, records, staffing, systems and remedies into a coherent order.

26.1.2 The minimum elements of an operational legal system

An operational system needs more than an Act. It needs commenced instruments; appointed and delegated decision-makers; published forms and service standards; an authoritative register; licensed firms; supervisory data; enforceable customer-asset rules; investigations; reasons; complaints; appeals; judicial review; and resources. The minimum sequence is set out below.

Figure 26.1 — From legal text to a reviewable controlled legal knowledge architecture

![Figure 26.1 — From legal text to a reviewable controlled legal knowledge architecture](Assets/Figures/Figure-26.1-Publication-v025-v3.png)

No stage can safely be inferred from the existence of the previous one. Notification proves legal publication; it does not prove staffing, supervisory coverage or customer redress.

26.1.3 Bottom line and design principles

Pakistan does not need another declaration that digital assets matter. It needs a controlled conversion of enacted law into an operable legal order. The Virtual Assets Act 2026 (VAA) has already supplied a federal regulator, a functional service perimeter, licensing and issuer modules, customer-asset duties, preventive and supervisory powers, offences, an appellate design and delegated-law powers. The preceding chapters nevertheless show that enactment and operability are not the same thing. A statute can be in force while the entry route is transitional, the final rulebook remains incomplete, a cross-regulator boundary is unresolved, an institution has not been authenticated, or a remedy cannot yet be exercised predictably.ch26-26-r406

The corrective package therefore begins from law already enacted. It does not treat the field as a clean slate, reproduce the Act in subordinate legislation or replace specialised regulators with a digital-asset super-regulator. It also does not ask regulated businesses to cure defects that belong to the State. A VASP can file a complete application, segregate customer assets and implement controls. It cannot appoint the Authority’s Board, establish a Tribunal, correct a statutory cross-reference, create a tax charge, allocate federal and provincial competence, or convert draft regulations into law. Those tasks must remain with the institutions legally empowered to perform them.

Eight principles govern the programme.

1. Legality before scale. No market-expansion target, public-wallet programme, mining allocation or tokenisation initiative should outrun the legal authority, customer protection, fiscal control and review mechanism applicable to it.

2. Instrument discipline. Parliament should decide essential policy, jurisdiction, coercive power, liability, tax and remedy. Federal Rules and PVARA Regulations should operationalise authority already conferred. Standards may specify testable technical requirements. Guidance may explain but must not create a disguised offence, licence condition or tax burden.

3. Function before label. The perimeter should turn on the legal and economic function actually performed, including control of assets, order execution, settlement, issuance, payment, investment intermediation and governance—not on names such as “utility token”, “protocol”, “DAO” or “decentralised”.

4. One decision, visible contributors. Where several regulators participate, one lawful decision-owner must be identifiable. Consultation does not transfer statutory power, and board membership does not merge mandates.

5. Transition without legal fiction. Continuity should protect customers and enable orderly applications. It should not imply that an NOC is a full licence, that a pending application is approved, or that a saved instrument is automatically valid for every Act-era purpose.

6. Proof, not promulgation alone. A Gazette notification is necessary where law requires it; it is not evidence that the regulated interface works. Completion requires authenticated instruments, named owners, working forms and data channels, trained decision-makers, tested remedies and published performance evidence.

7. Proportionality with a hard protective floor. Requirements may vary with activity, scale and risk, but segregation, governance, fitness, financial crime controls, truthful disclosure, operational resilience, reasons and access to review are not optional.

8. Revision by evidence. The regime should record incidents, supervisory findings, complaints, appeal outcomes, market concentration and implementation failures, and use them to revise subordinate instruments without concealing the version history.

This hierarchy is also a sequencing rule. An administrative form cannot cure missing statutory authority. A memorandum cannot decide a legal perimeter entrusted to Parliament or another regulator. A technical standard cannot impose a penalty not authorised by the Act. Conversely, Parliament need not hard-code every cryptographic control or data field. The reform succeeds when each question is placed at the lowest level that can lawfully and durably answer it, while every higher-order safeguard remains intact.ch26-26-r407

26.2 The Present Position of Citizens, Holders and Incumbent Providers

26.2.1 Current exposure, uncertainty and evidential burdens

Citizens may hold assets acquired through foreign platforms, peer-to-peer transactions, gifts, mining or other routes. Their immediate problems are evidential: identity of counterparties, acquisition cost, source of funds, wallet control, tax valuation and availability of records after platform failure. Holding, using, marketing, transmitting and operating a business are distinct. The law should not turn uncertainty in one category into a presumption about all the others.

26.2.2 Immediate need for authoritative public transition guidance

PVARA should publish one consolidated transition notice stating the commencement dates, activities requiring permission, treatment of existing complete applications, marketing restrictions, customer-asset duties, forms, fees, decision timelines, complaints route and consequences of refusal. SBP, SECP, FBR, FMU and relevant enforcement bodies should join or formally cross-reference the notice where their powers are affected. Frequently asked questions may explain the law but cannot enlarge it.

26.3 Legal Validity and the Authoritative Instruments Register

26.3.1 Commencement, appointments, delegations and review routes

For every power, the public record should show the enabling provision, commencement, office-holder, delegation, territorial scope, procedure and route of review. Delegations should identify the function and conditions rather than use generic internal authority. A decision made by the wrong person is not cured by its substantive attractiveness.

26.3.2 One authenticated and versioned public legal record

PVARA should maintain an authenticated, searchable register containing the Act, current Rules and Regulations, commencement instruments, delegations intended for publication, forms, fees, binding directions, general guidance, licence conditions of general application, amendments and superseded versions. Each item should carry source, date, legal status and effective period. A website upload without provenance should not be treated as law.

26.3.3 Publish the transition position

Section 70 gives an existing provider a six-month bridge only if it submits a complete licence application within the statutory period and complies with interim directions and core obligations. Section 74 saves specified pre-Act matters, while section 73 permits removal of difficulties for six months but not an order inconsistent with the Act. These provisions should not be collapsed into a general amnesty.ch26-26-r408 The exact terminal day should be confirmed by reasoned legal determination and officially published; this report does not manufacture certainty between 4 and 5 September 2026. The transition notice should state:

  • the class of provider capable of relying on section 70 and the evidence of existing activity;
  • what makes an application “complete”, how deficiencies are notified and whether a cured filing retains its original date;
  • the status of NOC holders, non-holders and applicants at each stage;
  • the obligations that apply during the bridge, including safeguarding, AML/CFT, disclosure, incident reporting and cooperation;
  • the consequences of rejection, withdrawal, incompleteness or expiry; and
  • customer-protection, transfer and wind-down requirements where authority to continue ends.

The notice must distinguish law from assistance. A checklist cannot extend the statutory period, and an NOC or pending application cannot be described as a licence. If the enacted transition cannot safely be completed, Parliament—not guidance—must alter it.

26.3.4 Authenticate appointments, delegations and decision authority

Before a body exercises coercive or determinative power, the public record should identify the lawful office-holder, appointment instrument, commencement date, term, vacancy status, delegation and any recusal. The Authority should publish a consolidated governance page linking the Board constitution, chairperson and member notifications, authorised committees, delegations under section 10, and the officers empowered to issue notices, decide applications, inspect, freeze, sanction or defend proceedings.ch26-26-r409 Sensitive personal material need not be exposed. Legal authority must be.

Delegation instruments should identify the source power, delegate, subject, conditions, duration and retained powers, and preserve non-delegable functions. Proof requires a public delegation register cross-checked against protected signature and access controls.

26.3.5 Establish or authenticate the review route

The Act’s Tribunal and direct appellate route raise the constitutional and procedural concerns analysed in Chapter 23. The immediate response cannot wait for the first contested freeze or licence refusal. Government should publish the legal instruments establishing the Appellate Tribunal, appointments and terms, seat and filing channel, registry, procedural rules, fee and service arrangements, interim-relief jurisdiction, case-allocation method and route for further review—or state candidly which elements remain unavailable.ch26-26-r410

Pending primary correction, every PVARA adverse decision should contain reasons, the legal source of power, the material relied on, the effective date, the available internal reconsideration (if any), and an accurate notice of the presently available remedy. That notice must not purport to exclude constitutional jurisdiction. If the statutory Tribunal is not operational, an agency webpage cannot pretend that it is; equally, an administrative complaints portal should not be presented as a substitute for adjudication.

26.3.6 Create the authoritative instruments register

The operative regime cannot be reconstructed from press releases, unversioned downloads and draft handbooks. PVARA should maintain a single public register containing the Act, saved instruments, Federal Rules, PVARA Regulations, Gazette references, commencement and repeal data, binding standards, non-binding guidance, general directions, consultation drafts, feedback statements, forms and superseded versions. Every item should show its legal basis, status, issuer, approval date, effective date and checksum. Drafts should carry a permanent watermark and cease to appear beside operative instruments without a status distinction.

This is not administrative polish. Publication and version control determine notice, reliance, equality of treatment and the evidence available to a court. As at the cut-off, PVARA’s official consultation page still describes the proposed Virtual Asset Services Regulations and activity handbooks as draft and subject to revision, while the licensing page states that full VASP licensing is “coming soon”.ch26-26-r411 The current official regulations page displays the Act, NOC material and ART sandbox documents; it does not establish that the consultation draft has become final law. The register should make that status impossible to misunderstand.

26.3.7 Issue a bounded continuity determination

Section 74 should be applied instrument by instrument. For each Ordinance-era NOC regulation, direction, application, order and institutional act, the responsible authority should record: the pre-Act source; whether the subject survives under the Act; whether the content is inconsistent; the new statutory home; any adaptation required; and the date on which it will be replaced. Where the Act requires consultation, Gazette publication or a different decision-maker, savings cannot be used to evade that requirement.

The determination should preserve customer protection and procedural continuity without declaring an NOC equivalent to a section 19 licence. Section 73 may remove a genuine implementation difficulty within its limited life, but it should not be used to add a regulated class, create a levy, enlarge a penalty, change appellate jurisdiction or rewrite the transition. Those are questions of legislative choice.

26.4 A Lawful Transition and Continuity Framework

26.4.1 Existing holders, own-account P2P users and incumbent providers

Section 70 of the Act gives an existing VASP six months from commencement to apply or cease; a person who files a complete application within time may continue the existing services pending determination, subject to interim directions and core obligations concerning customer assets and financial integrity.ch26-26-1 Regulation 5A gives operational detail, including prior approval for marketing during transition.ch26-26-2 That continuity is provider-, service-, time- and application-specific. It does not automatically cover a new service or an incomplete application.

26.4.2 No implied amnesty; any grace, safe harbour or regularisation must be express, bounded and legally valid

Neither transition language nor regulatory silence creates a general amnesty for earlier contraventions, untaxed gains or unexplained funds. Conversely, the absence of a general amnesty does not make every holder or own-account peer-to-peer user a VASP. Any regularisation route must state eligible persons, covered periods, disclosure, tax and AML treatment, exclusions, decision-maker, confidentiality, evidential effect and relation to criminal proceedings.

26.5 Primary Legislative Completion

26.5.1 Perimeter, issuers, customer assets and insolvency

The Act and Regulations should be tested for issues that delegated law cannot safely settle alone. Primary law should state the boundary with deposits, securities, derivatives and payment instruments; legal consequences of issuer redemption promises; recognition and transfer of digital assets; customer beneficial interests; segregation; reuse; shortfalls; priority; insolvency exclusion; and return or transfer. Criminal liability and compulsory deprivation also require clear legislative authority.

26.5.2 Enforcement, appeals, tax and regulator interfaces

Primary law should allocate investigation, administrative penalties, freezing, confiscation, compounding, appeals and judicial review with procedural safeguards. It should reconcile PVARA, SBP, SECP, FBR, FMU, FIA and provincial functions without implied transfer. Tax charge, valuation, withholding, information and regularisation cannot rest on regulatory guidance alone. A statutory interface mechanism should resolve classification without erasing each body's legal competence.

26.5.3 Clarify perimeter and regulator interfaces

The Act should preserve its functional service definition but add an express substance-first rule: characterisation under the VAA does not displace the law governing currency, deposits, payment systems, securities, derivatives, collective investment, companies, secured transactions, tax or underlying property. PVARA should classify the virtual-asset service; SBP, SECP and other competent authorities should decide questions Parliament has assigned to them. A joint determination mechanism should resolve mixed cases without allowing silence by one body to become approval by another.ch26-26-r412

The amendment should authorise a public perimeter register recording anonymised or publishable determinations, the facts treated as decisive, participating agencies and resulting permissions. It should also state the Pakistan nexus for remote and cross-border offerings: targeted solicitation, local distribution, local-currency access, local establishment, material local customer base or other objectively specified connection. A reverse-solicitation exception, if adopted, must be narrow, evidenced and unavailable where the provider cultivates the Pakistan market.

26.5.4 Complete the issuer lifecycle

Sections 18–23, 30–33, 42–43 and Schedule I do not yet supply an entirely clear route for the person issuing on its own behalf. Parliament should distinguish a principal issuer from a professional third-party issuance service provider and prohibit public offering, admission or targeted distribution without the appropriate approval. The statute should confer express power to require a white paper or equivalent disclosure, identify the legally responsible issuer, control marketing, impose continuing disclosure, require redemption or reserve arrangements where promised, and suspend or withdraw an offering.ch26-26-r413

The primary text should state the legal consequences of material misstatement, omission, unauthorised offering and failure to honour redemption. It should identify who may claim, the limitation framework, available compensation or rescission, and the relationship with securities and company law. It should not validate an “asset-referenced”, “stable”, “Shariah-compliant” or “real-world-asset” claim by name alone. Where a token represents title, a security interest or a beneficial interest, the underlying law must recognise and perfect that right.

26.5.5 Make customer-asset protection portable across insolvency

Section 24 already establishes segregation, fiduciary responsibility and exclusion of customer assets from the VASP’s estate. The amendment should make the protective consequences executable across custody chains and insolvency forums. It should address sub-custody, omnibus holdings, shortfalls, reconciliation, tracing, permitted lien or set-off, customer consent, return in specie, valuation where return is impossible, and recognition by liquidators and courts.ch26-26-r414

The legislation should authorise a Pakistani-law statutory trust or equivalent proprietary mechanism so ownership, control, priority and return can be proved when a VASP fails. Reuse or encumbrance should require authority, informed consent, activity-specific permission and clear loss allocation.

26.5.6 Repair AML/CFT allocation and the issuer gap

The VAA should identify PVARA’s AML/CFT supervisory role in terms aligned with the Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010 and the lawful designation architecture, without compromising the Financial Monitoring Unit’s protected functions. If the relevant Schedule IV allocation or notification has not been validly made and published, it should be made through the instrument required by the AMLA. The VAA’s reference to “FMLI” should be corrected to the legally intended institution.ch26-26-r415

The reporting-entity position of principal issuers and other covered participants should be stated expressly rather than inferred from a VASP definition designed around services to third parties. Parliament should confer power for risk-based treatment of self-hosted addresses, unhosted transfers, privacy-enhancing features and cross-border originator/beneficiary information, while preserving legality, proportionality, data minimisation, confidentiality and effective challenge.

26.5.7 Correct enforcement, penalty and appellate architecture

The amendment should implement the Chapter 23 enforcement chain: a single notice architecture; particularised grounds; access to adverse material subject to lawful protection; opportunity to respond except for justified urgent interim action; time-bounded freezes and restrictions; prompt confirmation; reasons; internal reconsideration where appropriate; and effective independent review. Sections 57, 59, 60 and 62–65 require coordinated redrafting so that prohibited conduct, maximum exposure, review, condonation, stay, appellate route and the relationship with constitutional jurisdiction are intelligible.ch26-26-r416

The law should distinguish administrative, civil and criminal routes; prohibit double punishment for the same wrong; and state how settlement affects other proceedings. Digital-evidence and key-custody powers require defined thresholds, records, proportionality, return and remedy. Penalties should not import an unlimited maximum from “any other law”.

26.5.8 Correct public-finance, tax and textual defects

Sections 13–15 and the annual-report provision should be aligned with the Constitution, the Public Finance Management Act 2019, federal accounting, audit and appropriation requirements. The amendment should clarify the legal status, custody, permitted application and reporting of the PVARA Fund; retain Auditor-General and parliamentary visibility; and prevent fees or monetary penalties from becoming an off-budget operational incentive.ch26-26-r417

Section 66’s reference to the “Income Tax Act” should be corrected to the Income Tax Ordinance 2001. The correction must not be mistaken for creation of a tax charge. Any digital-asset charging, withholding, reporting, valuation or loss rule belongs in the relevant fiscal legislation enacted under the constitutional allocation of taxing power.ch26-26-r418 The Act’s numbering and cross-references should be technically corrected, including the annual-report sequence. Section 70 should be amended only if the transition truly cannot be completed lawfully; section 74 should remain a savings provision, not a permanent substitute for Act-era instruments.

Finally, Parliament should decide—not leave to a handbook—whether and how the Authority’s Shariah advisory function relates to a token or product presented as Shariah-compliant. The statute need not make the regulator a religious certifier. It should prevent misleading claims, identify any recognised approval process and preserve the powers of financial-sector regulators whose laws govern the underlying product.

26.6 Federal Rules, PVARA Regulations and Guidance

26.6.1 Proper allocation among instruments

The instrument must match the proposition. Primary legislation should contain fundamental rights, charges, offences, coercive powers and institutional allocation. Federal Rules may organise matters entrusted to the Federal Government. PVARA Regulations may specify licensing, governance, capital, custody, reporting and conduct within delegated authority. Guidance may explain compliance and risk indicators but should not create a new offence, tax or licensing class.

Table 26.2 — Allocation of legal propositions by instrument

PropositionAppropriate vehicleReason
Property, insolvency priority, tax charge, offence, compulsory deprivationAct of ParliamentFundamental rights and liabilities require primary authority

26.6.2 Consultation, publication, commencement and version control

Consultation should publish the legal power, problem, proposed text, impact and response. Final instruments must be authenticated and notified as required, with a realistic commencement date and transitional provision. The notified 2026 Regulations—not earlier consultation drafts—control the present baseline. Every amendment should preserve historical versions so a person can identify the law applicable on a past date.

26.6.3 Federal Rules under section 67

Federal Rules should address matters assigned to the Federal Government or requiring government-wide procedural authority. The first Rules package should cover:

  • constitution and procedure of the Appellate Tribunal, to the extent the corrected Act lawfully permits;
  • appointment, terms, conflict management and vacancy handling where the Act leaves prescription to Rules;
  • Fund budgeting, accounts, custody, permitted expenditure, internal control, audit support and reporting;
  • lawful fees and prescribed monetary or procedural matters, without converting a fee into an unauthorised tax;
  • service of notices, authentication of instruments and certified electronic records across government interfaces;
  • the process for policy directions under section 71, including Gazette publication and an operational-autonomy assessment; and
  • any prescribed coordination or reporting matter expressly placed with the Federal Government.

Rules should not reproduce the entire licensing handbook. Nor should they be used to decide matters that the Act assigns to PVARA by Regulation. The responsible Division should publish an enabling-power concordance and obtain legal vetting before approval. Completion means Gazette publication, effective date, accessible consolidated text, forms capable of use and the institutional arrangements required by the Rules—not approval of a file note alone.

26.6.4 PVARA Regulations under section 68

The final Regulations should provide the binding operational rulebook. They should be modular enough to update a custody control without reopening unrelated mining or advisory rules, but integrated enough to avoid contradictory definitions and duplicated sanctions. At minimum, the stack should contain:

  • General/licensing: classification, completeness, fitness, ownership, governance, outsourcing, change, surrender, wind-down and public status;
  • Activity permissions: the Schedule I services and any lawfully added category;
  • Prudential: capital, liquidity, insurance, concentration, stress and recovery calibrated to activity;
  • Customer assets: segregation, records, reconciliation, keys, sub-custody, shortfalls and return;
  • Conduct/disclosure: customer treatment, conflicts, execution, fees, complaints, marketing, listing and continuing disclosure;
  • Market integrity: surveillance, records, confidential information, manipulation, listing conflicts and algorithmic-token controls;
  • AML/CFT and sanctions: risk, CDD, beneficial ownership, monitoring, reporting, sanctions and Travel Rule;
  • Technology/data/resilience: governance, access, change, third parties, incidents, continuity, recovery, evidence and privacy;
  • Regulatory reporting: identifiers, prudential, transaction, asset, incident and complaint data with correction history; and
  • Cross-border: Pakistan nexus, foreign conditions, group supervision, data access, reliance and exit.
  • Section 68 publication correction: amend the Act expressly to require Gazette publication, authentication and a stated commencement rule for Regulations; until then, describe the consequence as contestable rather than universally void;

The final text should state which provisions apply during transition and when new duties commence. It should include proportionate bands but preserve minimum duties. It should identify the source and maximum consequence of non-compliance rather than create a free-standing punitive code. Where a handbook contains a mandatory rule, that rule should migrate into the Regulation or a standard validly incorporated under it.

26.6.5 Standards and technical specifications

Standards are appropriate for matters that require precision and controlled revision: Travel Rule message fields and interoperability; customer-asset reconciliation files; wallet-control evidence; cybersecurity baselines; incident categories; application data dictionaries; regulatory returns; proof-of-reserve methodology if used; algorithmic-token stress scenarios; and audit-log retention. Each binding standard should identify the enabling Regulation, version, effective date, change log, conformance test and exception process.

Technical requirements should be outcome-linked. “Use industry-standard security” is not testable. A useful standard states the protected outcome, minimum control, evidence required, test frequency, severity classification and time to remediate. Where several implementations can achieve the result, the standard should avoid locking the market into a named commercial vendor or a cryptographic method that cannot be revised safely.

26.6.6 Guidance, supervisory statements and forms

Guidance should explain how PVARA interprets and administers the law, give worked examples and disclose supervisory expectations. It should say that it is non-binding, identify the provisions explained and state that a materially different lawful method can be demonstrated. A regulated person should not be sanctioned merely for departing from guidance where it complies with the binding rule and achieves the required outcome.

Forms and portals should collect only information lawfully required. Each field should map to an assessment or reporting purpose; sensitive information should have a retention, access and deletion rule. Portal validation should distinguish a technically accepted upload from a legally complete application. Automated risk scores may support triage but should not become undisclosed decision criteria.

26.6.7 Consultation and commencement controls

Before finalisation, PVARA should publish a disposition table showing material comments, accepted or rejected recommendation, reason, and textual consequence. It should perform an authority review, constitutional-rights review, competition and small-provider impact assessment, privacy and cybersecurity assessment, implementation-cost estimate and regulator-capacity test. If a rule cannot be supervised at commencement, that is a design defect, not a reason to pretend compliance can be inferred.

The final package should use staged commencement. Governance, fitness, customer-asset, AML/CFT, disclosure, incident-notification and records duties should apply first or remain continuously applicable. Requirements dependent on new schemas or systems may commence after published conformance testing. Grandfathering should protect orderly transition, not exempt inherited business indefinitely. PVARA should publish the signed final instruments, Gazette evidence where applicable, a clean text and a redline against the consultation draft.ch26-26-r420
