26.15.9 Regulatory data, interoperability, privacy and evidence

A rule model is only as reliable as its source and input data. Interoperability should therefore begin with identifiers and meaning, not bulk data transfer. The system needs stable identifiers for instruments, provisions, organisations, licences, permissions, officers, applications, evidence items, decisions, cases and model releases. Each shared field requires a definition, lawful purpose, source custodian, validation rule, time quality and correction route.

The Digital Nation Pakistan Act defines digital public infrastructure to include identity, data exchange, cloud and open-data components and gives the Pakistan Digital Authority important standards and coordination functions. It also preserves control and responsibility of designated data custodians and expressly requires avoidance of overlap with other regulatory mandates.ch26-26-r464 That supports a common technical layer; it does not create permission for PVARA, PDA or a vendor to collect or combine any dataset that would be useful.

The data architecture should use minimum disclosure. An eligibility or perimeter query often requires verification of a proposition rather than disclosure of the underlying record. A system may need to know that a company exists and that a representative holds a valid role, not retrieve every filing or personal identifier. Access should be role-based and purpose-limited; sensitive evidence should be encrypted, logged and segregated; test data should be synthetic or lawfully de-identified; and public rule models should not expose investigative thresholds whose disclosure would defeat a lawful function.

Chapter 23 established that data protection, cybersecurity and evidence are separate legal questions. A secure database can still be unlawful; a lawful collection can still be insecure; and an accurate system log can still require proof of attribution and integrity. Qānūn-Map should preserve the source of an input, who supplied or changed it, when it was valid, the method of verification and any contest. Hashes and digital signatures can assist integrity and authentication, but they cannot prove that the original factual assertion was true.ch26-26-r465

Evidence exports must be intelligible without the live system. A decision file should contain the operative source text or stable official locator, all relevant versions, inputs, provenance, branch path, reasons, human approvals, notices and later changes in a durable format. Retention must follow legal purpose and proceedings, not the convenience of indefinite storage. A person should be able to correct an erroneous factual record without rewriting the historical fact that the earlier decision used it.

Interoperability also requires graceful failure. If an identity, company, tax, sanctions or regulator interface is unavailable, the service should show the failure and offer a lawful alternative. “No response from another database” must not be translated into “not eligible” or “non-compliant”. Cross-agency APIs should carry status and timestamp, not just values, and each institution must remain responsible for the field it authoritatively maintains.

26.15.10 Human authority, explanation and contestability

Human control is not satisfied by placing an officer after an automated result if the officer lacks time, evidence, training or authority to depart from it. Meaningful human judgment requires the power to ask for more information, change a classification, refuse the model’s recommendation, record reasons and trigger correction of a defective rule. The reviewer must know which parts were calculated and which were legal or factual assumptions.

The workflow must also guard against automation bias. A prominently displayed score or “recommended outcome” may become functionally decisive even when a form permits override. Assurance should therefore examine actual override rates, time available for review, whether officers receive the underlying evidence rather than only the output, and whether departures attract inappropriate managerial pressure. For contested or adverse cases, the interface should present the legal question and evidence before any system recommendation, so that the officer forms an independent view.

The Constitution requires public power to be exercised through law, fair process and legally responsible institutions. The VAA allocates classification and licensing functions to PVARA, requires written reasons for refusal at the NOC stage and provides an appellate structure for persons aggrieved by Authority orders.ch26-26-r466 Software cannot become the statutory Authority, an appellate tribunal or the Supreme Court. Nor can a generic “human in the loop” transfer one regulator’s power to another institution.

Every result that may affect a person should disclose:

1. the purpose and non-binding or binding status of the process;

2. the source instruments and exact versions used;

3. the material facts supplied, retrieved or inferred;

4. the rule path and calculations;

5. missing information, conflicts, `[DRAFT]` and `[GAP]` states;

6. the responsible institution and named or identifiable decision function;

7. the human reasons for any operative decision;

8. how to correct facts, make representations and obtain the record; and

9. the complaint, review, appeal or court route available under law.

Explanation should track the actual decision. A generic statement that “requirements were not met” is not cured by attaching hundreds of rules. The officer should identify the decisive legal provision, factual finding, evidence accepted or rejected, treatment of a material representation and consequence selected. Where security or investigation law justifies withholding particular information, the limitation itself needs authority and review; secrecy should not become the default explanation for system opacity.

No automated tool should make or execute an adverse legal decision merely because its prediction is accurate on historical data. Prediction and authority are different. Historical outcomes may encode inconsistent administration, exclusion or error. A machine-learning score may help prioritise a review only under an approved purpose and assurance regime; it should not supply an undisclosed substantive criterion. For the bounded programme proposed here, the preferable core is transparent deterministic logic, with analytics kept separate and never allowed to overwrite the legal rule path.

Contestability also improves the model. Successful challenges, withdrawn decisions and unusual cases should enter the regression suite after legal review. That does not mean that a single officer’s decision rewrites the law. It means the programme tests whether the model omitted an exception, misrepresented an ambiguity, relied on poor data or invited users to answer a legal conclusion as if it were a simple fact.

A remedy must remain usable outside the platform. Loss of an account, service outage or inaccessible interface cannot extinguish a statutory time limit or right to make representations. Notices should identify an alternative channel, and the complete record should be obtainable in a durable human-readable form. The reviewing institution should be able to suspend reliance on a disputed model without disabling the underlying legal process.

26.15.11 Governance, assurance and controlled change

Qānūn-Map requires institutional governance before scale. The minimum operating model separates five roles: the authoritative-source custodian; the legal-model owner; the responsible regulatory decision owner; the engineering and security owner; and an assurance function able to stop release. The same person or vendor should not authenticate the law, interpret it, write the implementation, approve it and certify the result.

Each model release should pass six gates:

GateRequired proof
sourceauthenticated instrument, status, dates, hierarchy and amendment check
legal mappingprovision-by-provision derivation, unresolved interpretations and competent owner
datadefinitions, lawful access, provenance, correction, quality and privacy assessment
technicalreviewed code, pinned dependencies, security tests, reproducible build and rollback
casesordinary, boundary, missing, conflict, draft, gap, adversarial and prohibited-outcome tests
administrativeauthorised use, trained officer, reasons template, notice, record and working remedy

The inspected demonstrator also supplies five concrete pre-pilot defects for those gates. Its engine is imported from another research workspace and must be pinned, reviewed and hashed within an approved build. Its exclusion and connected-perimeter inputs are Boolean values although they are legal conclusions requiring an identified officer, evidence, reasons and validity period. Its exclusion predicate cites sections 3 and 5 although the principal express exclusions appear in section 2(2), so the map must be corrected and regression-tested. Its generic `hcc_required` flag does not allocate user, clerical, legal, inter-regulator, override and final-decision roles. Its notice should distinguish tentative screening output from a final, binding or statutory legal determination.

The test suite is a legal-control asset. It should include cases in which the correct output is “unknown”, “wrong institution”, “draft only”, “source conflict”, “human classification”, “insufficient authority” or “do not proceed”. A system tested only on clear approvals will predictably treat ambiguity as approval. A system tested only on enforcement cases will over-route ordinary activity as risk.

Change control should use dual approval by legal and technical owners. A source update triggers an impact report identifying affected rules, tests, services and prior cases. Material changes require notice and, where rights or duties change, the legal process required for the underlying instrument—not only a software release. Rollback must restore the last approved model and preserve decisions already taken for review. The audit log must include rejected releases and emergency overrides.

Procurement cannot outsource responsibility. A contract should require open data and rule formats where lawful, documentation, source and dependency disclosure, portability, security obligations, incident notice, audit access, exit assistance and continued access to decision records. Proprietary code must not prevent PVARA, a tribunal or a court from understanding the basis of a public decision. Vendor performance claims and laboratory accuracy are not evidence of lawful deployment.

Governance should include conflicts and participation. Regulated firms may properly test whether a rule model reflects operational reality, but they should not control the interpretation, acceptance tests or release decision for requirements that bind them. Applicants, customers, affected communities, lawyers, accessibility specialists and frontline officers should be able to expose burdens and edge cases through a recorded process. Consultation evidence should be published or summarised with reasons, while confidential and security-sensitive material remains protected under identified authority.

Independent assurance should sample source pinpoints, reproduce results, challenge edge cases, inspect access and change logs, test the remedy and ask whether the system has become functionally mandatory despite being described as optional. Material incidents include not only cyber compromise but use of a draft as operative law, a stale model, inability to explain a result, systematic override by staff, data drift, inaccessible review and any automatic adverse consequence outside authority.

Programme metrics should measure legal and administrative quality: source defects found, unresolved gaps, disagreement categories, corrected inputs, time and cost to complete the lawful process, successful challenges, security events and remedy availability. A high number of automated completions is not success if people cannot understand or contest them. The assurance function should report residual defects and have a defined suspension threshold.

26.15.12 National Digital Masterplan integration and institutional ownership

The Digital Nation Pakistan Act provides the planning and coordination setting for a future programme. The National Digital Commission approves the Masterplan and provides strategic direction. The Pakistan Digital Authority develops, implements, monitors and periodically updates it; coordinates across governments and regulators; develops technology standards and reference architectures; and monitors alignment. The Act requires sectoral and implementation plans, consultation, milestones and annual review.ch26-26-r467

That framework can supply the horizontal layer: source and metadata standards, reference architecture, identity and data-exchange conventions, accessibility, cloud and security baselines, procurement patterns and programme monitoring. It does not make PDA the VAA decision-maker. Section 8(g) itself requires avoidance of overlap and conflict with other regulatory mandates. PVARA remains the vertical legal owner of VAA perimeter, licensing and supervision; SBP, SECP, FMU, FBR and other institutions remain owners of their respective law.

The institutional design should be recorded in the relevant sectoral and implementation plan, with budget, staff, milestones, risks, assurance and public outcome measures. A technical reference architecture without these owners would repeat the implementation gap the Masterplan is intended to address.

FunctionProposed accountable ownerBoundary
cross-government legal-data and service standardPDA under an approved Masterplan/valid instrumenttechnical coordination; no sector decision transfer
VAA source and obligation modelPVARA legal owner with Gazette/source custodian supportonly operative VAA material may drive live use
connected financial perimetereach competent regulator, through a recorded coordination processconcurrence or referral does not erase statutory competence
model engineering and operationapproved public team or procured supplier under institutional controlsupplier does not own legal interpretation or public decision
assurancefunctionally independent legal, technical, security and administrative reviewersauthority to stop or suspend release
public reportingPDA for programme indicators; each regulator for decisions and outcomes within its lawaggregated reporting must preserve privacy and legal status

Before an institutional shadow pilot and again before scale, a capacity-and-value gate should test whether the service improves rather than duplicates administration. The baseline should record current processing time, error and rework categories, officer time, unresolved referrals, applicant burden and cost. The pilot should identify which clerical or deterministic tasks it can actually complete, the expected percentage and volume of human escalations, required legal and technical staffing, source-maintenance cost, service levels and operating cost per case. If nearly every case receives another full review, the system adds delay without reducing legal risk. The programme should then narrow the use case, redesign it or stop. Progress requires an adopted benefit threshold and a termination rule, not an assumption that more digitisation equals more capacity.

At the evidence cut-off, the official National Digital Masterplan material reviewed by this report evidenced consultation and roadmap development, not an approved digital-assets Rules-as-Code sector plan.ch26-26-r468 The proposed programme must therefore be described as a recommendation for possible inclusion through the Act’s approval and consultation process. Neither this report nor its demonstrator is the Masterplan.

Section 28 of the Digital Nation Pakistan Act also requires care. Its override provision preserves stronger data-rights and cybersecurity measures, and persistent conflicts are to be addressed through consultation, Commission action within law or proposed legislative amendment. It is not a machine rule allowing a shared platform to select the “higher” institutional mandate or transfer PVARA, SBP, SECP, FBR or judicial powers to PDA.ch26-26-r469

26.15.13 A phased demonstration programme—and the limit of execution

The programme should advance by evidence gates, not by announcing a national platform and filling it later.

Phase 0 — source integrity. Establish authenticated source registers for the VAA, valid subordinate instruments and directly connected law. Assign provision identifiers, status, commencement, amendment and official-location metadata. Publicly separate operative, draft, historical and missing material. No executable case outcome is required.

Phase 1 — controlled research prototype. Refactor the existing perimeter screen into a self-contained, reproducible package. Replace legal-conclusion checkboxes with human determination objects. Add missing-input, draft, gap, cross-regulator and source-change cases. Publish the rule map, limitations and test results as research. Success is faithful traceability and safe escalation, not approval accuracy.

Phase 2 — institutional shadow pilot. With PVARA and connected institutions’ approval, trained officers run the model alongside—not inside—the live process. It cannot affect an applicant. Compare its questions and routing with human files; record disagreement; test privacy, security, accessibility and record export; and verify that the real review route works.

Phase 3 — legal validation. Responsible institutions approve a bounded rule set, use, version and reasons protocol through the appropriate legal and administrative instruments. Independent reviewers test authority, source fidelity, edge cases, data and prohibited outcomes. Any `[GAP]` that controls the result prevents progression.

Phase 4 — bounded public assistance and scale decision. A public service may explain the perimeter, collect an evidence inventory and route a user to the competent process. It should not issue a compliance badge or licence. Scale occurs only after measured reduction in error or burden, no material rights or security defect, demonstrable human override, working remedies, sustainable ownership and a reasoned Commission/sector decision under existing law.

The stop rules are as important as the phases. Code must never decide whether Parliament conferred a power; resolve an unresolved conflict between statutes; determine a contested legal character solely from a label; find dishonesty or liability; impose a sanction; freeze property; grant, refuse, suspend or revoke a licence; decide proportionality; dispose of an appeal; or prevent a court from examining legality. It may assemble the record, identify the question, calculate a formally determinate element, display alternatives and expose missing proof. The judgment and legal act remain with the authorised human institution.

This boundary is not hostility to technology. It is the condition for trustworthy technology in public law. Code supplies precision, reproducibility and the capacity to test implementation. Law supplies authority, rights, limits, reasons and remedy. Capital supplies capability and exposure: the resources to build systems, the incentives that may distort them, and the losses distributed when they fail. Intelligent order is achieved when each is made visible to the others without being allowed to impersonate them.

Pakistan’s contribution need not be the largest automated regulatory platform. It can be more important: a model of machine-legible administration in which the source is authenticated, drafts cannot masquerade as law, gaps stop false certainty, every branch is traceable, institutions retain their lawful competence, adverse decisions remain reasoned and reviewable, and correction improves both text and implementation. That is how a National Digital Masterplan can move toward machine-executable regulation without making regulation machine-sovereign.

26.16 Implementation Horizons

26.16.1 Now: legality, continuity and public notice

The immediate horizon is the validity and transition layer: publish the authoritative register and transition notice; confirm appointments and delegations; identify complete incumbent applications; enforce core custody and AML duties; publish forms, fees, standards and contacts; and open complaints and review channels.

26.16.2 Next: operational completion

The next horizon is licensing decisions and institutional completion: conduct fit-and-proper and system reviews; establish supervisory reporting; agree SBP-SECP-PVARA protocols; enact necessary primary-law repairs; operationalise custody, tax and data requirements; train investigators and courts; and test firm wind-down plans.

26.16.3 Then: evaluated scale, interoperability and consolidation

Only after evidence of lawful operation should Pakistan expand product classes, cross-border recognition, tokenised public or private instruments and machine-readable services. Scale should follow measured market integrity, inclusion, resilience and redress. Consolidation should repeal superseded text and simplify interfaces without weakening rights.

26.16.4 Horizon I — Now: legality and continuity

The immediate horizon should complete the transition determination, authenticate governance and delegations, publish the instruments register, verify the Tribunal and investigation routes, finalise the section 74 continuity matrix, and establish the programme board and issue log. Government should settle drafting instructions for the targeted amendment Bill and Federal Rules. PVARA should dispose of consultation comments, publish its legal-authority concordance and identify which final regulatory modules can lawfully commence under the enacted Act.

Concurrently, the perimeter intake, AML allocation, tax taxonomy, provincial-tax and mining workstreams should begin. Existing customer-asset, AML/CFT, disclosure, records and incident duties remain applicable to the extent grounded in current law and valid instruments.

Horizon I requires authorised decision-makers, public status, a completeness method, an accurate appeal notice, protected incident contact and approved dependency report. A meeting is not completion.

26.16.5 Horizon II — Next: operational completion

Once the legal foundations are secure, Parliament and Government should progress the amendment Bill and Federal Rules through their lawful processes. PVARA should make the final Regulations, standards, forms and staged commencement package. Institutions should staff and test authorisation, supervision, customer-asset, market-surveillance, AML, cyber, enforcement, complaints and Tribunal workflows. Joint bodies should decide the model perimeter cases and publish permissible portions.

Every transition applicant should receive an evidenced status and continuity plan. Permission-based licensing and first-cycle supervision should test assets, key control, AML/Travel Rule operations, incidents, resources and wind-down, followed by remediation or lawful restriction.

Horizon II requires an accessible consistent rulebook, tested portals and schemas, a Tribunal test case, reasoned cross-regulator referrals, reconstructable customer assets and a candid first implementation report.

26.16.6 Horizon III — Then: evaluated scale and consolidation

Only after reliable operating evidence should the State expand sandboxes, rely on selected foreign evidence or scale public-use, mining and tokenisation initiatives. Incident, complaint, concentration, loss, AML, fiscal and performance data should control expansion; failing products remain capped, restricted or prohibited.

Government should commission an independent twelve-month implementation review measured from full operational commencement, not merely from the Act’s enactment. The review should examine legality, institutional independence, perimeter disputes, licensing quality, customer-asset failures, financial crime outcomes, data and cyber incidents, tax administration, remedies, costs, competition and innovation. Parliament should receive the report and the responsible institutions’ response. A later statutory review can determine whether a consolidated Act, further amendment or accepted residual risk is justified.

Some residual risks may be accepted, monitored or studied where law is valid, safeguards operate and reasons are recorded. Unresolved authority, customer ownership, coercive process, tax, institutional validity and remedy remain legality gates. Scale should follow operating evidence, not innovation vocabulary.

26.17 Future Scenarios and Anticipatory Legal Intelligence

26.17.1 Market, technology, geopolitical and institutional scenarios

Pakistan should prepare for at least four scenario families: rapid retail adoption; institutional tokenisation and stablecoin settlement; cross-border restrictions or sanctions shocks; and a major custodian, protocol or cyber failure. Scenarios are not forecasts. They expose legal dependencies, concentration and choices that should be made before crisis.

26.17.2 Triggers, safeguards and revision pathways

Triggers should be observable—customer-asset shortfall, redemption stress, market concentration, cyber severity, illicit-finance indicators, court invalidation or supervisory overload. Each trigger needs a lawful decision-maker, available measures, rights safeguards and sunset or review. Emergency power should not become a permanent substitute for legislation.

Table 26.4 — Scenario triggers, lawful response and review

TriggerInitial lawful responseMandatory safeguardRevision question
Custodian shortfallPreserve records and assets; restrict withdrawals only under authority; activate transfer or insolvency planReasons, proportionality, customer notice, court accessAre segregation and shortfall rules adequate?
Stablecoin redemption stressVerify reserves and liabilities; coordinate with SBP; apply issuer conditionsNo public guarantee without authority; equal treatment of claimantsIs the instrument inside the correct monetary perimeter?
Severe cyber incidentIsolate affected systems; preserve evidence; require recovery reportingData minimisation, chain of custody, service-restoration prioritiesDo resilience and outsourcing rules require amendment?
Cross-border enforcement conflictIdentify competing laws; preserve assets and data lawfully; use cooperation channelsConfidentiality, affected-person process, judicial supervisionAre connecting rules and agreements sufficient?

26.17.3 Scenario method, horizon and uncertainty

The purpose of foresight in this report is not to predict which token will succeed, how many Pakistanis will use a wallet, or when a global market cycle will turn. Its purpose is to expose decisions that become dangerous if they are first considered during a run, a failure, a constitutional challenge or a rapid shift in market structure. This chapter supplied the corrective package. § 26.17 asks whether that package remains usable when plausible conditions diverge from the assumptions under which it was drafted.

Figure 26.5 — Scenario matrix

![Figure 26.5 — Scenario matrix](Assets/Figures/Figure-26.5-Publication-v025-v3.png)

The scenarios use two planning horizons measured from a formally adopted implementation start. The operational horizon covers the period in which legal instruments, licensing, interfaces, supervisory systems and remedies are being made functional. The structural horizon covers the later period in which scale, concentration, new technical forms or changed international standards may test the architecture. These are not statutory deadlines. No probability is assigned, and no scenario is selected as the “expected” future.

Each scenario is constructed from seven elements:

1. an explicit assumption about market, technology or institutional conditions;

2. the law, institution or operational dependency placed under stress;

3. the mechanism by which the system could fail or produce unequal loss;

4. the persons, rights, assets and public interests affected;

5. safeguards already present in law or proposed in this chapter;

6. the residual risk after those safeguards; and

7. an observable indicator that should trigger review before the failure becomes acute.

The stress ratings used below describe consequence if the scenario occurs, not likelihood. “Low” means the stress is secondary and contained by ordinary controls. “Moderate” means the architecture should cope if this chapter controls operate. “High” means failure of one control can cause material harm. “Critical” means the scenario can defeat several safeguards or expose unresolved authority, property, public finance or remedy. Uncertainty is preserved, not hidden in a confidence score.

Pakistan’s starting point is neither prohibition nor a completed market. The VAA is operative and already supplies functional scope, licensing, customer-asset, issuer, AML/CFT, enforcement and delegated-law architecture. But the official record reviewed at the cut-off still describes the comprehensive VASP Regulations as draft, the NOC stage as current and full licensing as forthcoming.ch26-26-r437 That starting condition matters: a future scenario cannot be tested honestly by assuming that every this chapter correction has already been enacted or implemented.

International materials confirm that implementation variability is itself a future driver. The FSB’s 2025 thematic review records progress but significant gaps and inconsistencies, particularly for global stablecoin arrangements and cross-border coordination.ch26-26-r438 FATF’s 2025 update likewise identifies continuing difficulty with offshore VASPs, persons exercising control in DeFi, stablecoins, fraud, recovery and Travel Rule implementation.ch26-26-r439 These findings do not forecast Pakistan’s market. They justify testing a domestic regime against cross-border activity, functional ambiguity and uneven foreign cooperation.

The matrix is deliberately divergent. A completed licensing framework may coexist with a stablecoin run. Tokenisation may grow while unbacked trading contracts. Cross-border rules may harmonise in one function and fragment in another. The useful result is not a single narrative. It is a set of conditions under which a regulator, court, ministry or legislature knows what evidence to watch and what decision it must be prepared to make.

26.17.4 Baseline order: prolonged incompleteness

Assumption. The VAA remains operative, NOC and transition cases continue to require administration, final regulatory modules or connected instruments arrive unevenly, and a material share of customer activity remains offshore or outside a clearly evidenced domestic permission. This is a continuation scenario, not a claim that delay will occur.

The legal stress is produced by time. An NOC, pending application, sandbox permission, saved Ordinance-era instrument and statutory licence are different legal states. If the public register, completeness method, transition determination, appointment record and review route remain incomplete, repeated administrative practice may harden into market expectation without acquiring legal authority. Banks, customers and foreign counterparties may then rely on inconsistent descriptions of who is permitted to do what.

The affected interests are broader than applicants. Customers may believe that regulatory engagement equals full supervision. Compliant firms may bear higher costs than offshore competitors. Banks may either over-exclude legitimate applicants or supply access without a complete regulatory status. PVARA staff may be asked to decide under criteria not yet contained in valid instruments. A court may receive an urgent dispute before the Tribunal, record-transfer process or digital-asset custody mechanism is demonstrably operational.

Current law is not empty during this scenario. Direct statutory duties concerning unauthorised activity, customer assets, conduct, AML/CFT, cooperation and enforcement remain relevant according to their terms.ch26-26-r440 The danger is selective operability: coercive powers may be invoked before corresponding procedures, reasons and remedies work; businesses may face duties without a usable application path; or customers may receive warnings without a practical return or complaint route.

The no-regret response is therefore this chapter’s Horizon I package: publish exact status; authenticate appointments and delegations; maintain the authoritative instruments register; verify the lawful review and investigation routes; decide section 74 continuity instrument by instrument; and state which requirements apply during transition. Government should progress only those measures for which authority and implementation capacity are proved. It should not compensate for delay by presenting a draft handbook as binding or by announcing scale targets.

Early indicators. The dashboard should watch the age and legal status of NOC and licence applications; number of publicly unclassified providers; frequency of banks requesting regulator confirmation; customer complaints caused by status confusion; unpublished or superseded documents still used in decisions; vacancies and unverified delegations; inability to file an appeal; and the proportion of supervisory actions later withdrawn for procedural reasons.

Residual risk and implication. Even a candid transition notice cannot eliminate litigation over accrued positions or the exact operation of section 70. The design implication is to preserve customer continuity while refusing legal fiction. If the baseline persists, the response is targeted amendment or a lawfully made instrument—not indefinite administrative tolerance. Uncertainty: neither the duration of incomplete implementation nor the scale of offshore substitution can be responsibly quantified from the verified record.

26.17.5 Regulated-market deepening

Assumption. The amendment, Rules and final Regulations contemplated by this chapter are substantially completed; PVARA grants activity-specific permissions; banks supply controlled account access; and supervised domestic providers begin to mediate a greater range of customer activity. This scenario tests success conditions rather than assuming that authorisation itself is success.

The first stress is supervisory load. A licence converts a prospective assessment into a continuing obligation to supervise ownership, governance, capital, custody, conduct, AML/CFT, technology, outsourcing and wind-down. If licence issuance outpaces trained staff, reliable returns and inspection capability, the system may create a stronger appearance of safety than the evidence warrants. The risk increases if a small number of exchanges, custodians, banks, cloud providers or analytics vendors become essential across the market.

The second stress is multi-function concentration. An exchange may combine brokerage, custody, lending, proprietary dealing, token listing, settlement, staking and issuance support. Legal-entity approval cannot erase conflicts between these functions. Customer assets may support settlement exposure; proprietary trading may influence listing or execution; and group entities may shift risk beyond the licensed perimeter. The FSB and IOSCO frameworks both treat functional coverage, conflicts, data and cross-border cooperation as necessary parts of implementation rather than consequences that follow automatically from licensing.ch26-26-r441

The third stress is connected-law dependency. A PVARA permission cannot supply SBP payment or foreign-exchange authority, SECP securities authority, FBR tax treatment, provincial services-tax treatment, property title or an environmental approval. Market deepening therefore tests the joint perimeter and referral mechanism more severely than a small transitional market. A delayed decision by one institution can block a lawful product; an informal concurrence can expose all institutions to challenge.

This chapter remains resilient if licences carry a machine- and human-readable permission schedule; every provider has a named supervisory owner; capital and customer assets are independently reconciled; material outsourcing and group exposure are mapped; cross-regulator determinations are published; and an exercised wind-down route exists. Expansion should be sequenced by risk, with custody, exchange, lending, leverage, payment and issuer permissions subject to stronger evidence than low-footprint advice.

The market should not be measured by licence count alone. Early indicators include assets and customers per provider; share of custody, liquidity, cloud and banking dependencies concentrated in the largest entities; capital exceptions; reconciliation breaks; complaints per activity; unresolved perimeter referrals; frequency and age of prudential remediation; staff-to-risk ratios; and the proportion of providers capable of completing an exit exercise. A rapid increase in licensed volume combined with flat supervisory coverage is an escalation trigger, not a success indicator.

Residual risk and implication. Regulation can shift risk rather than remove it: into concentrated providers, shared infrastructure, group entities or customer belief in State guarantee. The legal design should therefore preserve resolution, portability and failure planning from the first licence. Uncertainty: the verified record does not establish the future number, scale, ownership or business model of licensed providers, or the degree to which Pakistani customers will move from offshore channels.

26.17.6 Stablecoin and payment stress

Assumption. One or more fiat- or asset-referenced tokens become materially used by Pakistani customers for conversion, remittance, merchant settlement, savings-like balances, DeFi collateral or cross-border trade. The scenario does not assume that such use is lawful in every form, that a token is legal tender, or that adoption reaches any numerical threshold.

Stablecoin scale compresses several legal events into a fast technical path: acquisition with rupees or foreign currency; custody or self-hosting; cross-border transfer; conversion; payment instruction; merchant settlement; reserve redemption; and accounting or tax recognition. Different institutions may own each decision. The VAA provides fiat- and asset-referenced categories and issuer/reserve architecture, but SBP retains currency, banking, payment and foreign-exchange authority under its laws. Contractual acceptance by a merchant does not convert the token into legal tender or settle the legality of the conversion and payment legs.

Three failure mechanisms should be tested. First, an issuer run may arise from doubt about reserve quality, custody, legal title, redemption, banking access or sanctions. Secondly, a gateway interruption may prevent conversion or merchant settlement even where the token continues to trade on-chain. Thirdly, a cross-border integrity shock may cause foreign issuers, banks or platforms to freeze addresses or restrict a jurisdiction, leaving customers with an asset they cannot lawfully or practically redeem.

The financial-integrity stress is substantial. FATF’s 2025 update reports increasing illicit use of stablecoins, continuing offshore-VASP challenges and weak recovery after major thefts; its revised Recommendation 16 also changes international payment-transparency expectations.ch26-26-r442 These are global observations, not findings about Pakistani users. They justify a system capable of identifying originator, beneficiary, provider, self-hosted address risk and lawful freeze or rejection without treating every stablecoin transfer as illicit.

The monetary and prudential stress is different. BIS’s 2026 analysis recognises tokenisation’s potential while concluding that current stablecoin arrangements do not supply all foundational properties of money and may create integrity and macro-financial challenges at scale.ch26-26-r443 For Pakistan, the relevant question is not whether a foreign report prefers another monetary architecture. It is whether reserve, redemption, liquidity, currency substitution, FX, settlement and loss allocation can be governed under Pakistani law.

This chapter’s FRT module should therefore be tested before material retail or payment scale. The test requires a legally identified issuer; holder claim; reserve ownership, custody, composition and valuation; daily or risk-based reconciliation; redemption time and suspension grounds; payment and FX permissions; customer-money treatment; settlement finality; refunds and chargebacks; AML/Travel Rule interoperability; insolvency; and a coordinated run plan. A reserve attestation without liability, control and redemption evidence is insufficient.

Early indicators. Authorities should monitor, under lawful data powers, stablecoin exposure by provider and use rather than publicity estimates; concentration by issuer, reserve custodian and blockchain; redemption requests and delay; deviations from the promised reference; changes in issuer terms; bank or gateway interruptions; use as DeFi collateral; self-hosted and cross-border transfer patterns; sanctions or freezing events; customer complaints about convertibility; and differences between on-chain supply evidence and provider liabilities.

Residual risk and implication. Pakistan cannot compel a foreign issuer, reserve bank or blockchain to continue service. Domestic rules can limit exposure, require local accountability, preserve evidence and create an exit route, but cannot guarantee parity. The legal design implication is to cap or condition retail, payment or public-sector reliance until redemption and failure tests pass, and to require SBP–PVARA–FMU coordination before crisis. Uncertainty: future stablecoin use, reserve location, issuer cooperation and the speed of a confidence shock are unknown; no adoption or loss figure is forecast.

26.17.7 Tokenised assets and capital-market expansion

Assumption. Regulated firms or public bodies pilot or offer tokenised shares, debt, fund interests, commodities, warehouse goods, land-related claims or other real-world assets. Demand may come from domestic investors, diaspora, institutions or cross-border platforms, but the scenario assigns no volume or success probability.

Tokenisation can reduce reconciliation friction and make transfer conditions programmable, but it also creates a second representation of a legal right. The central stress is divergence: the token ledger shows one holder while the company register, depository, land record, warehouse document, secured-transactions registry or custodian record shows another. A technically final transfer may be legally ineffective; a valid court order may not propagate on-chain; or an oracle may report that an off-chain condition occurred when it did not.

The applicable law follows the underlying right and function. A token representing a share or investment may engage securities, company, depository and market-infrastructure law. A token purporting to represent land or goods depends on the law governing title, registration, possession and priority. The VAA can govern issuance services, virtual-asset conduct and custody, but it does not make every tokenised claim valid or displace SECP, registrar, provincial or judicial authority.ch26-26-r444

The stress chain should test six events: valid initial creation; disclosure and investor classification; transfer and settlement; corporate action or income distribution; creation and enforcement of a security interest; and issuer, custodian or platform insolvency. It should also test a lost key, erroneous transfer, fork, frozen wallet, fraudulent duplicate token and mismatch between token supply and legally outstanding rights.

This chapter’s issuer and RWA bridge remains adequate only if every project has a legal-rights memorandum and an authoritative-record design. The memorandum should identify issuer and obligor, holder’s enforceable claim, governing law, authoritative register, transfer formalities, restrictions, custody, perfection, priority, corporate actions, tax, enforcement and insolvency. The system should specify when the token ledger is authoritative, evidential or merely operational, and who can lawfully correct divergence.

International work supplies evidence of possibilities and preconditions, not Pakistani authority. BIS work on tokenisation identifies potential use in payments and financial transactions and emphasises the legal, governance and operational foundations needed for deployment.ch26-26-r445 The correct domestic pilot therefore links technical tests to a recognised asset and institutional owner. A sandbox decision cannot validate title, waive public procurement, or substitute for a securities approval.

Early indicators. The dashboard should record asset classes proposed; classification time; percentage of pilots with complete legal-rights memoranda; authoritative-register integration; reconciliation exceptions; corporate actions requiring manual correction; rejected or reversed transfers; custody concentration; secondary-market liquidity; investor complaints; and unresolved questions of perfection, tax or jurisdiction. A project should stop if the underlying registry cannot recognise or correct the tokenised state.

Residual risk and implication. Some legal rights may not be suitable for tokenisation without primary amendment or registry reform. Parallel records can increase, rather than reduce, operational complexity. The design implication is “registry before token”: identify the legal source of truth and correction authority before public issuance. Uncertainty: it is unknown which asset classes will present a lawful cost advantage over existing electronic systems, and no efficiency or capital-raising outcome is assumed.

26.17.8 DeFi, DAO and autonomous-agent diffusion

Assumption. Pakistani customers obtain material access to decentralised exchanges, lending pools, staking arrangements, DAO-governed services or AI systems that recommend, initiate or manage virtual-asset transactions. Access may occur through local interfaces, foreign applications, wallets, APIs or general-purpose agents. The scenario does not assume that a protocol is decentralised merely because its code is public or its governance uses tokens.

The first stress is factual attribution. A protocol may involve developers, deployers, interface operators, governance participants, oracle providers, administrators, multisignature signers, liquidity suppliers, fee recipients and users. Their legal significance differs. IOSCO’s DeFi work treats claims of decentralisation as facts to be examined through control, influence, economic interest and operational roles, while preserving the need to apply the relevant legal framework.ch26-26-r446 Pakistan should use those indicators to investigate, not to impose automatic developer or token-holder liability.

The second stress is authority. An automated system may form or perform a contract, route an order, rebalance assets, vote, borrow, liquidate collateral or transmit a payment. Pakistan’s Electronic Transactions Ordinance supports electronic form and attribution of automated communications to a person using or controlling the system, but attribution does not resolve consent, authority, mistake, fiduciary obligation, market conduct or remedy. The VAA’s functional definitions and control concepts may reach a service or issuer without conferring personality on code.ch26-26-r447

An AI agent sharpens this problem because it may select tools and actions not individually specified by the user. A provider could describe the output as information while the system actually personalises advice, exercises discretion or executes transactions. A customer may give a broad natural-language instruction that the agent converts into a chain of swaps, approvals and protocol interactions. The legal analysis must separate the user’s mandate, deployer’s design, model provider, wallet permission, interface, execution venue and any human override.

The third stress is common-mode behaviour. If many firms use the same model, data source, cloud service, oracle or agent framework, apparently independent decisions may become correlated. The FSB identifies third-party concentration, market correlation, cyber risk, model risk, data quality and governance as potential financial-system vulnerabilities from AI adoption.ch26-26-r448 In digital-asset markets, those vulnerabilities can combine with continuous trading, automated liquidation and thin liquidity.

This chapter’s functional perimeter remains resilient if final rules require an automated-system responsibility file. It should identify the legally accountable deployer; permitted task; customer mandate; activity classification; data and model dependencies; wallet and API permissions; transaction and value limits; testing; monitoring; override and shutdown; record of prompts, policy and actions where lawful; incident response; customer explanation; and remedy. The file should be proportionate, protect trade secrets and personal data, and preserve sufficient evidence to contest a decision.

DeFi regulation should focus on the accessible service and actual control. A local interface that selects assets, routes trades, controls fees or can suspend access may carry responsibilities even if it cannot alter the base protocol. An immutable protocol may still depend on an oracle, stablecoin, bridge, hosting layer or governance process. Conversely, writing code, holding a token or casting one vote should not be treated as conclusive proof of regulated control, partnership, agency or breach.

NIST’s 2026 concept paper on software and AI-agent identity and authorisation is expressly a draft project concept, not a legal standard, but it identifies a concrete design issue: autonomous systems need distinguishable identities and bounded access to data, tools and applications.ch26-26-r449 Pakistan should test agent credentials, least privilege, separation of customer accounts, revocation, transaction signing, human confirmation for defined actions and attribution logs before an agent receives custody or execution authority.

Early indicators. Relevant signals include material customer losses involving automated execution; growth in agent-controlled wallet permissions; common model, oracle, bridge or cloud dependencies; repeated overrides; actions outside mandate; unexplained correlated trading; prompt-injection or data-poisoning events; DAO administrator-key use; governance concentration; interface delisting or shutdown; and inability to reconstruct why and by whose authority a transaction occurred.

Residual risk and implication. Adaptive output cannot always be predicted or explained at transaction-level precision, and a foreign protocol may lack a reachable operator. The design implication is not a fictional electronic person. It is bounded authority, attributable deployment, observable control, intervention capacity, records and loss allocation. High-impact autonomous custody, execution or payment should remain restricted until those elements pass testing. Uncertainty: the capabilities, deployment patterns and genuine autonomy of future agents and protocols are unknown.

26.17.9 Cyber, fraud or institutional-failure shock

Assumption. A material event affects one or more critical providers or public institutions: compromise of signing keys; insider theft; corrupted entitlement data; cloud or telecommunications outage; bridge or oracle exploit; ransomware; coordinated fraud; reserve freeze; or absence of a lawfully authorised decision-maker during the event. The scenario is compound because digital-asset failures rarely respect institutional boundaries.

Figure 26.6 — Stress-test heat map

![Figure 26.6 — Stress-test heat map](Assets/Figures/Figure-26.6-Publication-v025-v3.png)

The first minutes produce an authority problem. Who can halt withdrawals, isolate a wallet, direct preservation, notify customers, obtain a court order, contact a foreign provider or decide that continued operation is unsafe? A technically capable person without lawful power may protect assets but contaminate evidence or infringe rights; a legally authorised official without keys, data or a working communication channel may be unable to act. Chapter 23’s authentication and responsibility protocol is therefore part of cyber resilience, not separate governance work.

The next phase produces a property and evidence problem. The provider must distinguish customer and house assets, valid and fraudulent instructions, on-chain and off-chain liabilities, frozen and lost assets, and recoverable and irrecoverable keys. Investigators need a preserved chain connecting system logs, wallet control, transaction data, device evidence and human decisions. Customers need accurate notice and access to funds that are not lawfully restricted. A premature public attribution can trigger withdrawals or prejudice proceedings; silence can deepen harm.

Fraud may exploit the same event. FATF’s 2025 update describes increasing fraud and scam exposure, major theft, stablecoin misuse and low recovery in a significant cross-border case.ch26-26-r450 These global findings do not measure Pakistan. They demonstrate why the plan must cover impersonation, false recovery services, compromised customer communications, mule accounts, dormant accounts and rapid layering after the original breach.

The this chapter package supplies four linked safeguards. First, the customer-asset and failure plan allows reconstruction and transfer. Secondly, the incident standard supplies severity, contacts, update duties and recovery evidence. Thirdly, the investigation SOP supplies preservation, key custody, legal process and return. Fourthly, the Tribunal and court route supplies interim relief and challenge. None is sufficient alone. A technically successful freeze without review can become unlawful deprivation; a perfect evidential chain without customer-asset records may prove the loss but not restore the asset.

The exercise should run without advance notice to the operational team while protecting live systems. It should simulate unavailable senior officers, a conflicted service provider, cross-border data, a disputed customer claim and an incorrect initial indicator. The after-action record should distinguish decision, authority, evidence, elapsed time, customer impact, failed dependency and remediation. Security-sensitive details can be protected, but the public should receive an accountable summary.

The heat map is a consequence comparison, not a probability map. Its central result is that the compound shock can defeat all modules simultaneously, while otherwise distinct scenarios repeatedly stress coordination and remedy. The common corrective priority is therefore a tested decision chain, not another general statement that cyber risk is important.

Early indicators. Signals include privileged-access anomalies; key-policy exceptions; unresolved reconciliation breaks; vendor or cloud concentration; repeated high-severity vulnerabilities; fraudulent domain and social-media impersonation; abrupt withdrawal or complaint spikes; delayed incident classification; inconsistent public statements; unavailable decision-makers; evidence-transfer failures; and orders that cannot be implemented by custodians or foreign platforms.

Residual risk and implication. No architecture prevents every theft, outage or fraud. Foreign recovery may fail, technical intervention may be unavailable, and compensation may not cover loss. The design implication is to minimise irreversible exposure, preserve lawful options and practise failure. Uncertainty: the initiating event, target, duration, asset-recovery rate and contagion path cannot be predicted and are not assigned probabilities.

26.17.10 Cross-border fragmentation or harmonisation

Assumption. Foreign jurisdictions continue to implement crypto-asset, stablecoin, tax, payment, sanctions, data and AI rules at different speeds. Some requirements converge through international standards while market-access, custody, issuer, privacy and enforcement rules remain incompatible. Pakistan may face both demands for recognition and restrictions by foreign providers.

The scenario stresses section 4 extraterritorial reach and sections 9 and 17 cooperation and recognition powers. An offshore platform may target Pakistan without a conventional establishment; a foreign issuer may serve local wallets but deny local jurisdiction; or a Pakistan licensee may depend on a custodian whose home regulator restricts service. Two authorities may demand inconsistent retention, disclosure, freezing or customer treatment. A memorandum can facilitate exchange but cannot create coercive power or extinguish a Pakistani remedy.

The FSB’s 2025 review identifies gaps and inconsistencies in implementation and the resulting opportunity for regulatory arbitrage.ch26-26-r451 FATF’s revised Recommendation 16 increases convergence around payment-message information, but international convergence does not itself decide Pakistan’s domestic authority, privacy safeguards or technical interface.ch26-26-r452 Tax reporting adds another lane: CARF-style exchange requires domestic fiscal authority, due diligence, secure systems and an international legal basis, not a PVARA licence alone.

This chapter’s issue-specific recognition model is robust if every reliance decision identifies the activity, comparable outcome, home supervisor, data and record access, customer-asset location, local service and complaint route, enforcement cooperation, transition and withdrawal. Recognition should reduce duplicate evidence only where cooperation works. Material retail, custody, payment or stablecoin exposure may require local conditions even when a foreign licence is respected for a limited function.

The contrary path—fragmentation—requires an exit playbook. PVARA should be able to identify affected customers, assets, dependencies and contractual rights; require notice and transfer; preserve records; coordinate with SBP, FMU, tax and enforcement bodies; and state what Pakistan can and cannot compel. An untested promise of international cooperation is not a safeguard.

Early indicators. The dashboard should track foreign legal changes affecting Pakistan access; rejected supervisory requests; delayed or incomplete Travel Rule messages; foreign licence restrictions; concentration in jurisdictions without effective cooperation; conflicts over data, sanctions or freezes; sudden terms-of-service changes; blocked redemptions or withdrawals; and growing targeted solicitation by unregistered offshore providers.

Residual risk and implication. Pakistan cannot harmonise foreign law unilaterally and should not trade away constitutional, monetary, tax or customer-protection requirements for nominal access. The design implication is selective interoperability with an executable withdrawal route. Uncertainty: foreign reforms, equivalence decisions, geopolitical conditions and provider cooperation are external variables; neither harmonisation nor fragmentation is presumed dominant.

26.17.11 Mining, energy and environmental pathway

Assumption. Public or private actors seek to expand virtual-asset mining because of claimed surplus generation, changing tariffs, investment proposals or new equipment economics—or existing operations contract or migrate when those conditions change. PVARA may regulate a mining-related virtual-asset service, but it does not allocate power, approve a connection, set a tariff or grant environmental permission.

The main stress is temporal mismatch. Electricity described as surplus at one hour, season or network location may have another use at a different time. A long-lived concession based on a short-lived surplus can shift grid, fuel, capacity, transmission or environmental cost to households, firms or public finance. Technology may also change the revenue per unit of energy before the State recovers infrastructure or fiscal cost.

International evidence establishes the materiality of energy and emissions, not Pakistan’s local balance. IMF analysis links crypto mining and data centres to growing electricity demand and environmental externalities and cautions against special fiscal treatment without accounting for grid and social cost.ch26-26-r453 Its global estimates and proposed tax rates are not transplanted into Pakistani law or treated as local measurements.

This chapter’s approval stack should govern every project: verified load and location; generation and transmission evidence; lawful connection and tariff; curtailment priority; metering; environmental screening and approval; water and equipment-disposal effects where material; land and local permission; tax and customs treatment; procurement or allocation authority; public-money control; employment and technology claims; and termination if the factual premise changes. Provincial and federal institutions must act within their own laws.

Early indicators. Relevant signals are requested and connected load; hourly and seasonal utilisation; curtailment and grid congestion; tariff recovery and arrears; fuel and foreign-exchange exposure; emissions and environmental non-compliance; water or equipment-waste impacts; fiscal incentives; public infrastructure cost; jobs and local expenditure actually delivered; unauthorised mining; and divergence between projected and verified revenue.

Residual risk and implication. Even a compliant project may become uneconomic or impose opportunity costs when energy conditions change. The design implication is a reversible, measured permission—not a strategic entitlement. Uncertainty: future mining technology, asset economics, energy mix, location and genuinely available surplus are unknown; no public return is forecast.

26.17.12 Rights and distribution under the scenarios

None of the scenarios is distributionally neutral. The same control can protect one interest and burden another. Enhanced traceability may reduce fraud but expose financial associations; a rapid freeze may preserve assets but restrict innocent property; high capital requirements may protect customers but concentrate the market; local-presence rules may improve remedy but exclude a useful foreign service; and mining revenue may benefit one region while electricity or environmental cost falls elsewhere.

The constitutional frame remains legality, fair treatment, privacy and dignity, economic freedom subject to law, property, equality, information, federal distribution of authority and effective judicial review. These rights do not decide every policy outcome, but they require lawful source, rational classification, proportionality where rights are restricted, reasons and remedy.ch26-26-r454

The rights test must occur at design and incident stages. A lawful data field can become disproportionate when retained indefinitely or shared for a new purpose. An emergency restriction can become unlawful when urgency ends. An algorithmic risk score can support triage but should not become an undisclosed reason for licence refusal, account closure or enforcement. Human review must have authority and enough information to change the result.

Distribution should also be measured by who can exit. A sophisticated institution may diversify custodians, verify reserves and litigate abroad; a retail user may rely on a phone interface and regulatory badge. This chapter’s portability, reasons and remedy controls therefore protect capability, not merely formal equality. The National Digital Masterplan framework can coordinate inclusion and infrastructure, but it cannot authorise sector regulation or override rights.ch26-26-r455

Cross-scenario implication. The dashboard should disaggregate complaints, losses, freezes, service interruptions, licensing outcomes and remediation where lawful and statistically responsible. It should test whether burdens cluster by customer type, region, gender, disability, business size or access channel without turning protected data into a new risk. Uncertainty: distributional effects depend on actual use and institutional behaviour; no inclusion or employment benefit is presumed.

26.17.13 Decision triggers, early indicators and no-regret moves

Anticipatory intelligence becomes useful only when an indicator is connected to a lawful decision. A dashboard that reports rising stablecoin use but does not identify who can act, under what provision, with what evidence and remedy is market commentary, not governance. The this chapter implementation register should therefore add a scenario field to each corrective item: which future condition it protects against, what signal activates review and what response is available before primary law changes.

For this dashboard, three operational levels are proposed. Watch means an indicator changed and its lead must verify source and context. Where authority is absent, the response is amendment, court process, referral to the competent institution or limitation of a voluntary programme.

The threshold for an indicator should be adopted by the institution with legal and technical competence. Some can be numerical—capital, reconciliation tolerance or outage impact—once evidence exists. Others are necessarily qualitative: loss of a lawful decision-maker, inability to identify the holder’s claim, or conflict between two binding commands. The dashboard should show source, data quality, version and the reason an alert was opened or closed.

No-regret moves

Eight measures improve resilience across every scenario without presuming which one occurs:

1. maintain a public, versioned register of legal instruments, permissions, decisions and institutional authority;

2. make the PVARA–SBP–SECP–FMU perimeter and incident routes operational through test cases;

3. require reconstructable customer assets, liabilities, keys and dependencies, with an exercised return plan;

4. establish interoperable AML/Travel Rule and sanctions processes with privacy, correction and protected access;

5. authenticate the Tribunal, investigation and urgent-review routes before coercive crisis action;

6. record concentration in providers, banks, custodians, cloud, analytics, bridges, oracles and AI models;

7. run compound exercises that include legal, customer, communication, evidence and cross-border failure; and

8. publish outcome evidence and residual risk so that scale, restriction or legislative correction is reasoned.

These moves implement rather than enlarge this chapter. Their legal basis must still be identified item by item.ch26-26-r456 They should be reviewed quarterly at programme level, immediately after a material event and independently after the first full operational cycle. The review should preserve false alarms and rejected evidence; otherwise the State cannot learn whether its indicators are useful.

Handoff to 26.15 — machine-executable regulation

§ 26.15 should express the dashboard in machine-consumable form without allowing code to decide legal authority. Each indicator requires: stable identifier; source; status; effective version; data owner; condition; evidence or data-quality limitation—not scenario probability; accountable institution; lawful actions; mandatory consultation; safeguard; evidence; reasons; remedy; expiry and review. `[DRAFT]` and `[GAP]` states must block a system from presenting a proposed or absent rule as operative.

Agent identity and authorisation are suitable technical tests; statutory interpretation, proportionality, contested facts, institutional competence and remedy remain human legal judgments. International AI frameworks can inform governance, mapping, measurement and deactivation, but they do not allocate Pakistani power.ch26-26-r457 The machine-readable result should therefore generate a traceable alert and decision file, not an automatic freeze, licence refusal, tax charge or finding of liability.

The chapter’s conclusion is conditional but firm. Pakistan does not need to know which scenario will occur in order to make authority visible, protect customer assets, connect regulators, preserve evidence, test remedies and watch concentration. Those are no-regret foundations. The future question is not whether code, stablecoins, tokenisation or AI will inevitably transform finance. It is whether the legal order can recognise a material change early, identify the competent decision-maker, act within law, distribute loss fairly and revise itself on evidence.

26.18 Public Outcomes, Evidence and Accountability

26.18.1 Access, integrity, stability, innovation and rights

Success is not the number of licences or transaction volume. Relevant outcomes include safe access, market integrity, customer-asset recovery, payment resilience, lawful innovation, tax compliance, financial inclusion and protected rights. Trade-offs should be reported rather than hidden in a composite score.

26.18.2 Metrics, independent review and legal learning

PVARA should publish time-to-decision, refusal and appeal outcomes, complaints, asset shortfalls, incidents, enforcement disposition and market concentration with necessary confidentiality. Independent review should test both legality and effect. Lessons should lead to reasons, consultation and instrument change—not silent modification of forms or software.

26.18.3 Use a finance-sector implementation plan

The responsible federal Division should prepare a digital-assets sectoral implementation plan for Commission approval and Masterplan alignment. The plan should identify statutory outcomes, reform modules, owners, dependencies, resources, procurement, common infrastructure, indicators, risks, public reporting and review. PVARA, SBP, SECP, FMU, FBR, Law Division, relevant investigation bodies, provinces and the PDA should contribute within their mandates.

Each proposed national initiative should pass the twelve constitutional planning tests developed in Chapter 6: source of authority; lawful institution; federal–provincial competence; rights; public finance; procurement; data; cyber; regulatory perimeter; remedies; evidence; and revision. A label such as “national wallet”, “tokenised government asset”, “strategic reserve” or “mining hub” supplies none of those answers.

26.18.4 Separate regulatory foundations from market initiatives

The plan should contain two portfolios. The regulatory-foundation portfolio covers the amendment Bill, Rules, final Regulations, appointments, Tribunal, registers, interfaces, standards, capacity and tests. The market and public-use portfolio covers sandbox projects, tokenisation, payments, mining, investment promotion or public-sector uses. No initiative in the second portfolio should pass its scale gate until the applicable first-portfolio dependencies are complete.

For public-sector tokenisation or wallet use, the sponsoring institution must identify the legal asset, public-money flow, custodian, procurement, accounting, audit, cybersecurity, data, customer or citizen remedy, failure allocation and exit. A pilot should cap exposure and preserve an off-chain authoritative record where law requires. The State should not use a sandbox to avoid fiscal, procurement or constitutional control.

26.18.5 Align indicators with public outcomes

National reporting should distinguish inputs, outputs, operational outcomes and public outcomes. Staff hired and regulations issued are inputs and outputs. Accurate status, secure customer assets, reduced unresolved complaints, effective detection, predictable decisions, service recovery and lawful tax reporting are operational outcomes. Financial inclusion, investment quality, innovation, lower cross-border friction and reduced illicit finance are public outcomes that require evidence and counterfactual care.

The plan should publish baselines, definitions, source systems, frequency, owner and limitations. Commercial market estimates and chain-analytics outputs should be labelled as estimates. Regulatory data should not be repurposed for publicity without legal basis and quality review. The Commission’s monitoring record should disclose delayed dependencies and corrective decisions rather than convert every indicator into a success narrative.

At the evidence cut-off, official federal reporting described National Digital Masterplan consultations and implementation-roadmap work as ongoing. That supports active alignment work, not an inference that a final Commission-approved sector plan already exists.ch26-26-r434 This chapter therefore recommends the legal home and approval route; it does not invent approval.

26.19 The Final Proposition

26.19.1 A digital-asset order worthy of code, law and capital

Code can represent transactions and assist compliance; law allocates authority, rights and remedies; capital supplies productive risk-bearing. A credible order holds all three together. It allows innovation only through valid institutions and protects citizens without treating technological novelty as suspicion or immunity.

Figure 26.8 — Mandatory human escalation flow

![Figure 26.8 — Mandatory human escalation flow](Assets/Figures/Figure-26.8-Publication-v025-v3.png)

26.19.2 Authority remains human, public and legally accountable

The final safeguard is institutional responsibility. Legislatures enact; authorised regulators decide; courts adjudicate; firms remain accountable for their systems; citizens receive reasons and remedies. No dashboard, model, outsourced service or protocol should displace that chain. Pakistan's future order should become more intelligible through technology and remain governed by law.
